name: Russia–NATO
value: Russia warns Estonia of 'open war' 23 Nov
summary: Russia says Estonia is on the verge of triggering open war; NATO council met 23 Nov on missiles in Poland, no Article 4
state: On 23 Nov Russia's foreign ministry said Estonia was on the verge of triggering open war over hostile actions including its planned 1 Dec border closure; Tallinn denied letting Ukrainian drones use its airspace, and NATO's Rutte said the alliance is monitoring Estonia and Poland (Al Jazeera). NATO ambassadors held an extraordinary North Atlantic Council meeting on 23 Nov on the Kh-101 missile that fell in Poland on 20 Nov (United24). Poland's deputy defence minister said there was no need to invoke Article 4 (Reform.news). No Article 4 request or direct clash was found, so Watch holds.
for_you: No direct threat to the public in NATO states has been identified. Travellers to Poland and the Baltic states should check FCDO travel advice. Estonia plans to close its land border crossings with Russia from 1 Dec, which will affect overland travel.
rubric_hit: Watch: missile incursion into Poland (20 Nov) and explicit Russian threat against Estonia (23 Nov); no Article 4 invoked

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
